correctness.rationale: Incidence geometry gives distance two within a shore and distances one or three across shores. Hence higher names are singletons and a double occurrence of 2 must be a nonincident point-line pair. For a mixed independent set, the selected t lines avoid a selected point, giving 1<=t<=q^2. The incidence moments are (q+1)t and t(t+q), since every ordered pair of distinct lines meets once. Cauchy–Schwarz gives at least (q+1)^2 t/(t+q) covered points. Subtracting t gives at least q because the remaining numerator is (t-1)(q^2-t). This yields the sharp mixed bound v-q (a single line and all nonincident points attain it) and confines any independent set of size v-1 or v to one shore. Counting capacities first gives k>=v, then excludes k=v since a full color-1 shore would force the two color-2 vertices onto the same other shore. The exhibited type I uses v+1. At this optimum a missing higher name would force the same excluded sizes (v,2), so all higher names are used and the only low-class sizes are (v,1) and (v-1,2). These give types I and II exactly. The high-name vertices cannot move to 1 (each has at least q neighbors of color 1) or 2 (the incumbent 2 on their shore already blocks it). A move to another higher name duplicates a singleton. Type I therefore has just the q^2 choices of a nonincident 1 turning into 2; in type II, only the missing same-shore element can return to 1. The opposite-shore 2 cannot turn to 1 since it has color-1 neighbors. Thus every leaf has a unique parent and the counting factors 2v, (v-1)!, and 1+q^2 are exact. The Fano and order-three counts have the stated values.
residual_risks: The bounded programs were not run in this audit. The general proof uses only the plane axioms and applies conditionally on existence of a plane, for q>=2. The order-three reported computation is on configurations with singleton names forgotten, not the full named graph.

broader_coverage.reasoning: Incidence-free pair bounds are relevant to the independence step. The usual incidence matrix bound on an unbalanced pair (P',T) is (q+1)^2 |P'| |T| <= q(v-|P'|)(v-|T|), equivalent to |P'| <= v-(q+1)^2 |T|/(q+|T|), the moment bound used here. That follows directly by Cauchy–Schwarz on centered incidence vectors, since the incidence matrix has squared singular value q off constants. The gap and packing-class analysis should therefore not be treated as inventing a new geometric bound. No available source passage gives the subsequent packing classification or reachability classes.

equivalent_formulations.reasoning: Terminological aliases for packing colorings leave the claim unchanged. A dominated class instead requires a shared dominator, and cannot identify the packing states or their q^2 possible moves. Ordinary proper, distance-two and star coloring of the Heawood instance also do not impose distance thresholds depending on the color name.

value.rationale: The exact forest shows how individually movable 1/2-label choices coexist with global freezing of every higher name. It gives reachability, full counts and component diameters for a standard family, including planes without coordinates over a field. This is information not present in the chromatic number, an independence bound, or a census of two small planes.
residual_risks: The claim does not describe mobility with a spare color, name exchanges, or non-optimal intermediates.
